tagline: Golden domes over Roman streets — a Balkan capital where the metro runs through ancient ruins and a mountain looms over lunch.
overview: Sofia is one of Europe's oldest cities — a Roman provincial capital (Serdica) whose ruins surfaced when the metro was dug, now displayed in situ under glass in the city centre.

Above them rise the landmarks: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral's golden domes, the rotating guard of honour at the presidency, and the tiny 4th-century Rotunda of St. George tucked in a courtyard between ministries. Vitosha mountain — 2,290m — sits at the city's edge, with a chairlift starting in a residential neighbourhood.
Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Sofia. It remains one of Europe's cheapest capitals — meals, museums and mountains at Balkan prices, with the Rila Monastery UNESCO site a day trip south.

funFacts.title: ROMAN CITY UNDERFOOT
funFacts.text: The ancient city of Serdica lies under the centre — its streets cross a metro concourse.

funFacts.title: GOLDEN DOMES
funFacts.text: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral's domes are gold-plated — a memorial to Russian soldiers.

funFacts.title: A MOUNTAIN IN TOWN
funFacts.text: Vitosha's slopes start at the city edge — ski or hike after work.

funFacts.title: THE 4TH-CENTURY ROTUNDA
funFacts.text: St. George Rotunda, Sofia's oldest building, hides in a government courtyard.

funFacts.title: YELLOW BRICK ROAD
funFacts.text: The centre's famous yellow bricks were a gift from an Austro-Hungarian emperor.

funFacts.title: CHEAPEST EU CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Sofia routinely ranks as the European Union's most affordable capital.

funFacts.title: RILA MONASTERY
funFacts.text: The painted-striped 10th-century monastery is Bulgaria's UNESCO icon.
